messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] HIGH GPU QUEUE GROWTH - service: inference-redwood-prod - queue_length=~8200 -> throttling observed :rotating_light:
incident-bot: severity=sev2, runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-queue-exhaustion

Sara (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming impact: are customer requests hitting 503/429s?

Priya (customer-success): We have inbound notes from two customers seeing timeouts and slow responses on embeddings endpoints. Not full outage but heavy degradation.

Sara (oncall): Noted. Paging infra. @Mike (eng-infra) @Julia (eng-runtime) can you take a look?

Mike (eng-infra): ACK. Looking at autoscaler logs and ASG events. Will post findings shortly.

Julia (eng-runtime): I see queue depth spike on the GPU worker queue and a bunch of pods Pending due to node selector/taint constraints. Pods are stuck in ContainerCreating: "0/0 nodes available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod nodeSelector"

Mike (eng-infra): ASG attempted to launch 5 g4dn instances but they stayed in Pending with launch error. Cloud provider error excerpt:
```
2024-04-20T10:12:43Z Error: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ec2-instance-role
```

Mike (eng-infra): So autoscaler requested new nodes but launch template or instance profile change broke iam:PassRole. ASG hit scale limit while instances failed to initialize.

Alex (cloudops): Jumping in. Those launch template changes were rolled yesterday to rotate instance profile to new role. It looks like the role trust policy is fine but the autoscaling role lost iam:PassRole permission during a perms cleanup. I can restore but need 10-15m.

Sara (oncall): While Alex fixes IAM, we need short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact. Julia, can we drain non-critical GPU workloads and free nodes? Any safe sigkill?

Julia (eng-runtime): We have a mix: production inference pods (high priority) and batch finetune jobs (lower priority). I can cordon and drain nodes running batch jobs, and set replicas of low-priority deployments to 0. Commands I'll run:
```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
kubectl cordon ip-172-31-12-34
kubectl drain ip-172-31-12-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl scale deploy finetune-worker -n ai --replicas=0
```
I'll also remove tolerations/taints that might be preventing scheduling if safe.

Mike (eng-infra): Note: there are taints applied by the launch template: gpu-exclusive=true:NoSchedule. Some of our newer pods require that taint; older ones have tolerations. If new nodes come up with a different taint, runtime pod scheduling mismatches happen.

Julia (eng-runtime): Good point. For immediate relief I'll patch the inference deployment to tolerate the current taint and reduce max_batch_size to lower memory footprint so we can squeeze more pods per GPU. Patch commands:
```
kubectl patch deploy inference-prod -n inference -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu-exclusive","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
kubectl set env deployment/inference-prod -n inference MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8
```
This will increase concurrency but reduce per-request latency slightly — acceptable for now.

Priya (customer-success): I'll send a customer note: degraded latency on embeddings/generation endpoints; mitigation in progress.

Sara (oncall): Good. Also enable fallback to CPU-based small model for non-critical customers to reduce GPU load. Julia, is that a config flip?

Julia (eng-runtime): Yes. We have a routing flag per-tenant. I'll toggle it for tier=trial and tier=free. Patch config in console: set routing.fallback_model=cpu-small for those tenants.

Alex (cloudops): IAM fix applied. Restored iam:PassRole to autoscaling service role and re-ran launch. New instances are now transitioning to InService. Should see nodes register in k8s in ~2-3m.

CloudOps-bot: ASG event: desired=8, in-service=6, pending=2 -> instance i-0a1b2c3d initializing

Mike (eng-infra): Seeing nodes come up but one thing: launch template change also added a taint gpu-isolated=true:NoSchedule on new nodes. That prevents pods without the toleration from scheduling. Need to either remove taint on nodes or add toleration to pods. Which is safer?

Julia (eng-runtime): Easier to add toleration to inference-prod and autoscale groups via a pod patch (we already added gpu-exclusive toleration). I'll add another toleration for gpu-isolated:true to minimize mismatch.

Mike (eng-infra): Patching now. Command run:
```
kubectl patch deploy inference-prod -n inference --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu-isolated","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```
Should allow scheduling onto new nodes.

Sara (oncall): Any remaining blockers? Queue length trending down from 8200 -> 1200 after batch shutdown and routing changes. Still seeing occasional 503s for large requests.

Mike (eng-infra): One remaining issue: cluster autoscaler hit max node group size for the GPU node pool (current max=8). We discussed raising it during capacity planning but it wasn't increased. I've submitted a request to increase ASG max to 20; AWS update is in progress but may take 5-10m.

Alex (cloudops): Increase applied to ASG max-size -> 20. New scale requests will be honored.

CloudOps-bot: ASG scaling activity: increasing desired capacity from 8 to 14

Julia (eng-runtime): More nodes registering. Pod pending count dropping. I'm keeping watch on OOM/killed pods since we changed batch size.

Priya (customer-success): Customers updated. One large enterprise flagged significant latency but appreciates mitigation and is on standby for follow-up.

Sara (oncall): Good. I'm going to RIT-handoff to Mike for the next 60m while I rotate for lunch. Mike, please own the postmortem and next steps (launch template validation, IAM regression test, bump ASG max, improve taint/toleration docs).

Mike (eng-infra): Taking over. I'll gather logs and start a timeline. Immediate follow-ups I plan:
- Revert launch template drift or add automated policy checks to prevent iam:PassRole removal
- Add automated ASG max-size alert when nodepool reaches >80% of max
- Ensure new launch templates don't add surprising taints without a rollout entry in runtime config
- Add e2e test that spins a node with the launch template and registers to k8s

Julia (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a config rollout to make tolerations explicit per-deployment and add fallback-mode automatic routing when queue depth > 1000. Also add docs on safely draining GPUs.

Mike (eng-infra): Collating logs to S3 bucket s3://incidents/1713624800-gpu-autoscale/ and will attach in the postmortem.

Sara (oncall): Thanks all. Setting incident to monitoring, severity -> sev3 since customer impact is degraded but mitigations are active. Will update channel once postmortem draft is ready. :white_check_mark:

Priya (customer-success): I'll follow up with customers with ETA for full resolution and the postmortem when ready.

CloudOps-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=monitoring, severity=sev3, assigned=Mike (eng-infra)

Mike (eng-infra): Handoff notes saved. Next steps scheduled: IAM policy rollback verification, ASG max increase as permanent config, and an infra runbook update. Will file postmortem ticket PM-3421.

Sara (oncall): Back from lunch and confirmed queue stabilized at ~150. Thanks team.

Julia (eng-runtime): I'll follow up with a small canary to ensure config changes do not regress.

Priya (customer-success): Customers acknowledged. Closing proactive messages and will keep monitoring for 24h.

incident-bot: [CLOSE] incident moved to monitoring queue.
